faq.q: What is walk-forward validation in quantitative trading?
faq.a: Walk-forward validation is a testing methodology that repeatedly retrains and evaluates trading strategies on rolling time windows to ensure robustness and reduce overfitting in real-world market conditions.

faq.q: Why is walk-forward validation important for trading strategies?
faq.a: It helps prevent overfitting by simulating how strategies perform across different market regimes, ensuring that performance is consistent beyond a single historical dataset.

faq.q: How does walk-forward validation differ from traditional backtesting?
faq.a: Traditional backtesting evaluates a strategy on a fixed historical dataset, while walk-forward validation continuously re-optimizes and tests the strategy on sequential out-of-sample periods for more realistic performance assessment.

faq.q: Can walk-forward validation improve strategy profitability?
faq.a: Yes. By filtering out unstable or overfitted strategies, it improves the likelihood that deployed strategies perform consistently in live trading environments.

faq.q: Is walk-forward validation suitable for machine learning-based trading models?
faq.a: Yes. It is widely used in ML-based trading systems to evaluate model stability across time, reduce data leakage, and ensure generalization across market regimes.

faq.q: What skills are required for walk-forward validation experts?
faq.a: They typically require expertise in quantitative research, backtesting systems, statistical modeling, time-series analysis, Python, and financial data engineering.

faq.a: Microfrontends are an architectural approach where a frontend application is split into independently developed and deployed modules, enabling better scalability and team autonomy.

faq.q: When should a company use microfrontend architecture?
faq.a: Microfrontends are ideal for large-scale applications with multiple teams working on different parts of the UI, especially enterprise dashboards and complex SaaS platforms.

faq.q: What is Module Federation in microfrontend systems?
faq.a: Module Federation is a Webpack feature that allows multiple frontend applications to dynamically share and load modules at runtime across independently deployed systems.

faq.q: Do microfrontends increase application complexity?
faq.a: Yes, they introduce additional architectural complexity, but they significantly improve scalability, deployment independence, and long-term maintainability when implemented correctly.

faq.q: Can microfrontends work with React and Next.js?
faq.a: Yes. Microfrontends commonly use React, Next.js, and other modern frameworks with Module Federation or similar runtime composition techniques.

faq.q: How do microfrontends improve team productivity?
faq.a: They allow teams to work independently on separate UI modules, reducing codebase conflicts, enabling faster releases, and improving parallel development efficiency.

faq.q: What is microservices architecture used for?
faq.a: Microservices architecture is used to build large-scale backend systems by splitting applications into independent, deployable services that communicate over APIs or messaging systems.

faq.q: How do microservices improve system scalability?
faq.a: Microservices improve scalability by allowing individual services to scale independently based on demand, reducing bottlenecks and improving resource utilization.

faq.q: Do your microservices engineers work with event-driven systems?
faq.a: Yes. Our engineers design and implement event-driven architectures using tools like Kafka, message queues, and asynchronous processing pipelines.

faq.q: Can microservices be used with Kubernetes and Docker?
faq.a: Absolutely. Microservices are commonly deployed using Docker containers and orchestrated with Kubernetes for scalability, resilience, and automated deployment management.

faq.q: What challenges do microservices solve compared to monolithic systems?
faq.a: Microservices solve scaling limitations, deployment rigidity, and system coupling issues by breaking systems into modular, independently deployable services.

faq.q: Do microservices increase system complexity?
faq.a: Yes, microservices introduce additional complexity in networking, observability, and service coordination, but this is managed using orchestration tools, monitoring systems, and proper architecture design.
